template_name: Environmental Context-Dependent Memory Encoding and Retrieval
calibration_constraint: Reference SPATIAL-I SC1 parameters; avoid double-counting spatial navigation contribution

mechanism_chain.process: Hippocampal place cell ensemble generates a stable context representation of the current environment — a unique pattern of place cell activation that encodes the spatial configuration, sensory properties, and temporal state of the environment
mechanism_chain.substrate: Hippocampal CA1/CA3 place cells; grid cells and border cells in medial entorhinal cortex

data.finding: Hippocampal place cells fire at specific locations in environments; ensemble of place cells creates a unique 'context code' for each environment
Posterior medial system (including hippocampus, parahippocampal cortex) represents environmental context; distinct from anterior temporal object system

justification.backing: O'Keefe's discovery of place cells established that hippocampus represents spatial context. The place cell ensemble creates a unique fingerprint for each environment that serves as the neural basis for context-dependent memory.
justification.qualifier: Place cell coding is demonstrated in rodents; human evidence relies on fMRI pattern analysis which is less spatially precise.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human context representation differs fundamentally from rodent place cell system; but fMRI evidence supports hippocampal context coding in humans.

mechanism_chain.process: All experiences encoded in that environment are bound to the context representation. Episodic memory traces include both the content (what happened) and the context (where it happened) as an integrated relational binding.
mechanism_chain.substrate: CA1 relational binding; parahippocampal-hippocampal context pathway

data.finding: CA1 activation during encoding predicts subsequent relational memory (item-context binding)
Episodic memory is inherently contextual: what, where, and when are bound together in hippocampal trace
data.effect: Context is integral to episodic memory

justification.backing: Davachi's work established that CA1 binds items to their context during encoding. This relational binding means that experiences cannot be encoded in isolation — they are always embedded in the current environmental context.
justification.qualifier: The binding mechanism is established; the specific contribution of architectural features (vs. other contextual elements) to the binding is less precisely characterized.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if context binding is optional rather than automatic; but evidence supports automatic context encoding even when context is task-irrelevant.

mechanism_chain.process: Returning to the encoding environment reactivates the context representation. The reinstated context serves as a retrieval cue, facilitating access to all memories bound to that context (encoding specificity principle: Tulving & Thomson, 1973).
mechanism_chain.substrate: Hippocampal context reinstatement → pattern completion in CA3 → episodic retrieval

data.finding: Encoding specificity: memory is best when retrieval context matches encoding context
Context reinstatement reactivates hippocampal pattern from encoding, facilitating retrieval via pattern completion
data.source: Gordon et al. (2014); fMRI pattern reinstatement

justification.backing: Tulving's encoding specificity principle is the theoretical foundation for context-dependent memory. The mechanism is pattern completion: the reinstated context serves as a partial cue that triggers retrieval of the full memory trace.
justification.qualifier: The encoding specificity principle is robust; the specific environmental features that drive context reinstatement in architectural settings are inferred from general context research.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if mental context reinstatement (imagery) is as effective as physical return; but evidence shows physical context has added benefit.

mechanism_chain.process: Context-dependent memory advantage: recall is 20–40% better when retrieval occurs in the same environment as encoding vs. a different environment. The advantage is stronger for distinctive contexts.

data.finding: Meta-analysis shows 20-40% memory advantage for same-context vs. different-context retrieval
Classic underwater study: divers recalled words better when tested in same environment (underwater or land) as encoding

justification.backing: The context-dependent memory advantage is one of the most robust findings in memory research. The 20-40% effect size provides a quantitative basis for architectural applications: maintaining context stability between learning and recall improves retention.
justification.qualifier: Effect size varies by study and methodology; the advantage is larger for distinctive contexts and for recall (vs. recognition) tests.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if architectural changes (renovations, furniture moves) do not disrupt context sufficiently to impair retrieval; small changes may be tolerated via pattern completion.

hippocampal_encoding.interpretation: Recall is 20–40% better when tested in the same room/environment as encoding, relative to a different room. Meta-analytic estimate from Smith & Vela (2001).

context_stability_threshold.interpretation: If environmental context changes by <15% of weighted features between encoding and retrieval sessions, the context representation is still reactivated (pattern completion handles the discrepancy). Changes >15% reduce context reinstatement and impair retrieval.

environmental_novelty_level.interpretation: Highly distinctive environments (high dissimilarity from other known environments) produce stronger context-dependent retrieval advantages because the context representation is more unique and less susceptible to interference

spatial_configuration.interpretation: The spatial integration parameters from SPATIAL-I SC1 define the quality of the spatial cognitive map that serves as the substrate for context encoding. Do NOT re-calibrate spatial navigation parameters here — reference SC1 values directly.

age_group.effect: Context-dependent memory advantage is preserved in healthy aging but reduced in MCI/early AD due to hippocampal atrophy and pattern completion degradation

environmental_novelty_level.effect: Longer exposure to an environment produces a richer, more detailed context representation, increasing the retrieval advantage. Brief visits (<5 minutes) produce weaker context binding.

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Interoceptive state is PART of the context representation. The hippocampus encodes not just spatial context but also bodily state. This means that context-dependent retrieval is strongest when BOTH spatial environment AND bodily state match between encoding and retrieval (state-dependent memory). IC2 body budget interacts by shifting the interoceptive component of context.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Environmental control modulates the depth of context encoding: occupants with high perceived control explore more of the environment, producing richer spatial context representations and stronger context-dependent encoding. Low control restricts exploration and produces impoverished context representations.

cross_template_references: SPATIAL-I SC1 — provides spatial integration parameters; no double-counting
ED_HIPPOCAMPAL_ENCODING_001 — context encoding IS relational binding; these templates share the hippocampal CA1 binding mechanism
ED_PATTERN_SEP_COMP_001 — context distinctiveness depends on pattern separation of similar environments
SOCIAL-I SPATIAL_SOCIAL_ENCOUNTER_001 — social encounters encoded in spatial context; co-present persons become part of context representation

prefrontal_executive_control.interpretation: Maintaining consistent environmental features across encoding and retrieval sessions (same room assignment, consistent furniture layout, stable lighting) maximizes context-dependent retrieval

environmental_novelty_level.interpretation: Rooms that are distinctive relative to other rooms in the building produce stronger context binding and better context-dependent retrieval
